biological.citation: An Update on the Phenotype, Genotype and Neurobiology of ADCY5-Related Disease. (PMID: 33934385)
biological.summary: ADCY5 encodes adenylyl cyclase 5, the enzyme responsible for conversion of ATP to cAMP. ADCY5 is the most commonly expressed isoform of adenylyl cyclase in medium spiny neurons (MSNs) of the striatum and integrates and controls dopaminergic signaling. Through the cAMP pathway, ADCY5 is a key regulator of cortical and thalamic signaling that controls initiation of voluntary movements and prevention of involuntary movements. Gain-of-function mutations lead to dysregulation of the cAMP pathway, reduced inhibitory activity, and involuntary hyperkinetic movements.

biological.citation: New genetic loci implicated in fasting glucose homeostasis and their impact on type 2 diabetes risk. (PMID: 20081858)
biological.summary: GWAS meta-analysis of 46,186 nondiabetic participants identified ADCY5 as a novel locus associated with fasting glucose and HOMA-B (beta-cell function). ADCY5 was also demonstrated to be associated with type 2 diabetes risk. The locus contains a gene variant influencing signal transduction and glucose-sensing.
biological.sample_size: 46,186 nondiabetic participants with follow-up in 76,558 additional subjects

biological.citation: Requirement of Zebrafish Adcy3a and Adcy5 in Melanosome Dispersion and Melanocyte Stripe Formation. (PMID: 36430661)
biological.summary: In zebrafish, adcy3a-/- and adcy5-/- double mutants cause defects in melanosome dispersion and impair adult melanocyte stripe formation. Mechanistically, Adcy3a and Adcy5 regulate melanosome dispersion by activating kinesin-1 while inhibiting cytoplasmic dynein-1. In adult zebrafish, Adcy3a and Adcy5 regulate expression of Mitfa and melanin synthesis enzymes (Tyr, Dct, Trp1b). These proteins mediate α-MSH-MC1R/cAMP-PKA signaling.

biological.citation: PDE10A and ADCY5 mutations linked to molecular and microstructural basal ganglia pathology. (PMID: 30345538)
biological.summary: Striatal cAMP activity is determined by the balance between synthesis by ADCY5 and degradation by PDE10A. ADCY5 mutations were associated with decreased PDE10A expression in striatum and globus pallidus, decreased dopamine transporter expression in striatum, loss of substantia nigra neuromelanin-containing neurons, and microstructural white and gray matter changes within striatocortical pathways.
biological.sample_size: 6 subjects with PDE10A and ADCY5 mutations

biological.citation: ADCY5 gene expression in adipose tissue is related to obesity in men and mice. (PMID: 25793868)
biological.summary: In humans, visceral ADCY5 mRNA expression is significantly higher in obese compared to lean individuals and correlates with BMI, body fat mass, circulating leptin, fat distribution, waist and hip circumference. In mice, Adcy5 expression in adipose tissue is significantly higher after high-fat diet compared to chow. However, rs11708067 is not associated with ADCY5 mRNA expression levels in either fat depot, suggesting the SNP's T2D association may not be mediated through altered adipose tissue ADCY5 expression.

biological.citation: Genome-wide discovery of genetic loci that uncouple excess adiposity from its comorbidities. (PMID: 33619380)
biological.summary: GWAS identified 62 loci where the same allele is associated with higher adiposity and lower cardiometabolic risk. ADCY5 was prioritized as a gene affecting insulin-glucose signaling in adipocytes. The study suggests ADCY5 may represent a therapeutic target to reduce cardiometabolic risk linked to excess adiposity.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - A functional regulatory variant associated with type 2 diabetes and fasting glucose levels at the ADCY5 locus.
biological.summary: The rs11708067-A T2D risk allele shows decreased enhancer activity compared to rs11708067-G in luciferase reporter assays in 832/13 rat insulinoma cells (1.3 to 3-fold difference, p=0.0017-0.03). Allelic imbalance in H3K27ac ChIP-seq and differential protein binding in EMSAs support rs11708067-A as a functional variant. RNA-seq from 82 published and 32 new islet samples showed decreased ADCY5 expression for rs11708067-A (p=6.5×10⁻¹³).

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - An epigenetic switch confers pleiotropic risk for bone mineral density and hyperglycaemia.
biological.summary: In patient-derived osteoblasts and primary adipocytes, ADCY5 downregulation (mediated by loss of SREBF motif at rs56371916) leads to perturbation of fatty acid oxidation during early differentiation (3.6-fold, p=0.003) and failure to differentiate (2.9-fold change in alkaline phosphatase, p=0.0014). In adipocytes, ADCY5 downregulation decreases adrenergic lipolysis rate (1.9-fold, p=0.0012). CRISPR C-to-T editing restored ADCY5 activation and osteoblast differentiation.

Microarray analysis identified circAdcy5 as a heroin-responsive circular RNA in the rat orbitofrontal cortex after heroin self-administration. Linear Adcy5 mRNA levels were significantly changed by heroin exposure. circAdcy5 may impact cellular processes contributing to neurobiological adaptations from chronic heroin exposure through circRNA:microRNA sponging mechanisms.
biological.sample_size: Male and female rats with heroin self-administration

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - The impact of known type 2 diabetes associated variants on circulating levels of GLP-1, GIP and glucagon during an oral glucose tolerance test.
biological.summary: The ADCY5 rs11708067 risk allele was associated with increased incremental area under the curve (iAUC) of plasma glucagon from 0 to 30 minutes during OGTT (Beta [SE]: 0.130 [0.043], p=0.0025), showing reduced repression of glucagon release after an oral glucose load. This suggests ADCY5 variants affect alpha-cell function and glucagon secretion.
